subject_entity.notes: Gnostic teacher in Antioch c. 100–130, contemporary with Basilides. Taught that the world was made by seven angels; the God of the Jews was one of these angels. The Saviour was unborn, incorporeal, and only appeared to be human. Declared marriage and procreation to be inventions of Satan.

object_entity.proposition_label: Christ truly became flesh and truly suffered in the body
object_entity.description: The incarnate Christ was a genuine human being who truly was born, truly suffered, truly died, and truly rose again; not a phantom or appearance as the Docetists claimed.

evidence.notes: Irenaeus: the Saviour was unborn, incorporeal, and without form — only appeared to be a man.

passage.excerpt: Saturninus, who flourished at Antioch, set forth one father unknown to all, who made angels, archangels, powers, and potentates. The world was made by a company of seven angels. The Saviour he averred was unborn, incorporeal, and without form, but supposed to be a man in appearance only. The God of the Jews, he declared, was one of the angels. Marriage and generation, he maintained, are of Satan.
